entities.summary: Jordan of Saxony, OP, was a German Catholic priest and one of the first leaders of the Dominican Order. Born in the 12th century, he played a crucial role in the establishment of the Order in Europe. In 1221, he participated in the Second Council of Rome, where he collaborated with Pope Honorius III to define the Dominican Order's purpose and structure. This led to the creation of the first Dominican provinces and the appointment of the first Provincial Masters. Jordan of Saxony's legacy extends to the modern-day Catholic Church, where he is remembered as a key figure in the establishment of the Dominican Order. He is the patron saint of the Dominican Sisters, and his feast day is celebrated on February 13. As a prominent figure in the medieval Catholic Church, Jordan of Saxony's contributions had a lasting impact on the development of the Dominican Order and the Catholic Church as a whole. His commitment to the Order's mission and values has inspired generations of Dominicans, shaping the Order's identity and purpose. Through his leadership and vision, Jordan of Saxony helped to establish the Dominican Order as a major force in Catholicism, paving the way for its growth and expansion throughout Europe. As a result, his legacy continues to be felt today, with the Dominican Order remaining a significant presence in the Catholic Church.
